issues.legal_issue: A court with exclusive jurisdiction over a landlord’s claim for possession of leased land may grant incidental relief concerning structures when that relief is needed to make possession effective.
material_facts: The landlord sued the tenant for possession of leased plots under rent-control law and also sought possession of buildings erected on the plots.
The buildings stood on one plot; the other plot was vacant.
The landlord’s claim for possession of the leased plots succeeded, and relief concerning the buildings was sought as incidental to obtaining effective possession of the land.
issues.conclusion: The Small Causes Court had jurisdiction to hear the possession suit and grant incidental relief concerning the structures, including relief enabling delivery of vacant possession; seeking that relief did not require rejection of the whole suit.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28 of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947 gives the Small Causes Court jurisdiction over landlord–tenant suits concerning possession of covered premises and related claims. Importers and Manufacturers Ltd. v. Pheroze Framroze Taraporewala and Babulal Bhuramal v. Nandram Shivram support the breadth of that jurisdiction; Raizada Topandas v. M/s. Gorakhram Gokalchand is distinguishable because the pleadings there denied a landlord–tenant relationship, and Sushila Kashinath Dhonde v. Harilal Govindji Bhogani concerned claims arising under the Act. Ramachandra Raghunath Shirgaonkar v. Vishnu Balaji Hindalekar, Khimjee Thakorsee v. Pioneer Fibre Co. Ltd., and K. Arumugham Naicker v. Tiruvalluva Nainar Temple support treating removal of structures as incidental to effective delivery of land.

predicates.landlord_tenant_possession_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding against a tenant seeking possession of premises.
predicates.leased_premises_are_land: The premises at issue were leased land rather than the structures on it.
predicates.structure_relief_sought_to_make_possessi: The landlord sought relief concerning structures on the land as a means of making possession of the land effective.

issues.definition: When a landlord seeks possession of leased land from a tenant and relief concerning structures is sought to make that possession effective, the court with jurisdiction over the possession proceeding may grant that incidental relief.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant who persistently defaults and fails to meet the statutory conditions for protection is not entitled to rent-control protection from eviction.
material_facts: The tenant repeatedly defaulted in paying rent and taxes over a prolonged period.
After seeking time to deposit arrears, the tenant told the court that he could not make a deposit; the arrears were deposited only later, after the suit had proceeded to trial.
The courts below found persistent default and held that the tenant did not qualify for relief from eviction.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was not entitled to relief under section 12(3)(b) of the Bombay Rent Act, and the landlord was entitled to possession of the plots under the Act.
issues.legal_principle: The conditions in section 12(3)(b) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947 must be strictly observed to obtain its protection. Applying Ganpat Ladha v. Sashikant Vishnu Shinde, the Court held that a tenant who does not fulfil those conditions cannot claim the protection; persistent default and a clear statement of inability to pay excluded relief on these facts.

predicates.rent_control_ejectment_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking a tenant’s eviction under rent-control law.
predicates.persistent_rent_default: The tenant repeatedly failed to pay rent over a prolonged period.
predicates.tenant_admitted_inability_to_pay: The tenant told the court that he was unable to pay the arrears.
predicates.tenant_failed_to_deposit_arrears_diligen: The tenant did not deposit the arrears diligently and made the deposit only after substantial delay.

issues.definition: In a rent-control eviction proceeding, persistent rent default together with an admission of inability to pay or a failure to deposit arrears diligently results in denial of rent-control protection.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant who does not remove structures erected on leased land when the tenancy ends loses rights to those structures, and a landlord seeking possession may obtain relief needed to take effective possession of the land.
material_facts: The tenant had erected buildings on leased land under a lease that required the land to be returned free of structures.
The tenancy was terminated, and the tenant did not remove the buildings.
The landlord sought possession of the land and the buildings, and the Court affirmed the decree for possession.
issues.conclusion: The tenant lost rights to the structures by failing to remove them upon termination of the tenancy, and the landlord could seek the relief needed to obtain effective possession of the land, including removal of structures and vacant possession.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the principle, stated in Ramachandra Raghunath Shirgaonkar v. Vishnu Balaji Hindalekar and K. Arumugham Naicker v. Tiruvalluva Nainar Temple, that a tenant may remove structures on leased land when the tenancy ends but loses rights to structures left behind; a court’s power to deliver possession includes the incidental power to remove structures where necessary to deliver vacant possession.

rule.if: land_possession_proceeding and tenancy_ended and tenant_erected_structures and tenant_failed_to_remove_structures

predicates.land_possession_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking possession of leased land from a tenant.
predicates.tenancy_ended: The tenancy of the land had ended.
predicates.tenant_erected_structures: The tenant had erected structures on the leased land.
predicates.tenant_failed_to_remove_structures: The tenant did not remove the structures when the tenancy ended.

issues.definition: When a tenancy of land ends and the tenant leaves structures that the tenant erected, the landlord is entitled to effective possession, with the structures removable for vacant possession or retained as the landlord’s property.
